alignments.note: `ἐγένετο` rendered by the idiom *it came to pass*, headed on the verb word.
Expressed accusative subject of the infinitive.
Ordinary prepositional phrase of time, not an articular infinitive, so rule 61 is not in question.
`σάββασιν` rendered *sabbath day*; *day* is the supplied completion and the head stands on the word glossing the lexeme (rule 66).
The supplied complementizer *that* belongs to the non-finite complement the ASV expands into a finite clause (rule 85); discontinuous around the expressed subject under rule 15.

`ὁδὸν ποιεῖν` is a light-verb pair the ASV collapses into the single English verb *went* (its own margin gives the Greek as *to make their way*), so rule 73 keeps the two tokens in one unit with the supplied subordinator and subject riding inside under rules 7 and 86. Rule 39's test then sets the status: no part of the English answers to either lexeme, the corpus glossing `ὁδός` *way* and `ποιέω` *make* or *do*, which is rule 73's `noncompositional` arm as recorded for `ἔχουσα βασιλείαν` → *which reigneth*. Rule 10 puts the source head on the content-bearing noun and rule 17 the target head on the verb word. Reading the unit as `aligned` on the ground that *went* answers to the journey sense of `ὁδόν` remains defensible, but that is the same argument rule 73 declines for *reigneth*.
Participle rendered by an English infinitive; the marker is a rule 7 helper.

review_notes: Corrected the `ὁδὸν ποιεῖν` → *as they went* unit from `aligned` to `noncompositional`. Rule 73 sets the status by rule 39's test, and its `aligned` examples all show a visible lexical correspondence (*need* answers to `χρεία`); here neither *way* nor *make* stands anywhere in the English, which is the shape of the recorded `ἔχουσα βασιλείαν` → *which reigneth*. Membership and both heads are unchanged.

Everything else holds: `ἐν` → *on* is an ordinary temporal phrase and not an articular infinitive, so rule 85 rather than rule 61 places the supplied *that* on `παραπορεύεσθαι` — which is why this verse differs from MRK.2.15 without breaking rule 24.
`οἱ` before `μαθηταί` is `unrepresented` under rule 20, the genitive `αὐτοῦ` being free to carry *his*.
